question: Where did the devils ask not to go?
summary: Mark 5:9-10 has Legion beg Jesus not to send the demons 'out of the country.' Luke 8:30-31, telling the same story, has them beg not to be sent 'into the deep' (abyssos — the abyss). The geographic plea in Mark and the cosmological plea in Luke are not the same request.

reconcile.connective: Commentators read the two pleas as one request seen from two angles: the demons wanted to stay loose on earth — neither banished from that district (Mark) nor locked back in the abyssal prison (Luke).

discrepancy.connective: Critical scholarship presses the point that Luke's abyssos is a distinctive, apocalyptically loaded term absent from Mark's plainer 'out of the country' — evidence Luke is reworking his source rather than merely supplying a second facet of one utterance.

Falling back to Gill's own note on Luke 8:30, already surfaced on this row, which treats the passage directly and states the harmonization.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: …they desired, that when they went out of this man, they might not be ordered thither, or remanded to their former prison; for they knew that if he gave the word of command, they must obey; but that they might be suffered to continue in that country, and range about on earth, or be any where, rather than in hell.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Ties Luke's 'the deep'/'their former prison' (hell) to the demons' preference to 'continue in that country' — the same request Mark reports, read as two facets of one desire.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And they besought him,.... That is, all the devils, the whole legion of them, entreated Jesus, under whose power, and at whose dispose they were:
that he would not command them to go out into the deep; meaning, not the deep waters of the sea, for thither they ran the swine at their own request; but the bottomless pit of hell, where others of these spirits lay in chains of darkness; and so the Ethiopic version renders it, "into hell": they desired, that when they went out of this man, they might not be ordered thither, or remanded to their former prison; for they knew that if he gave the word of command, they must obey; but that they might be suffered to continue in that country, and range about on earth, or be any where, rather than in hell.
